T1.implementation_approach: Use a design tool like Figma or Adobe XD to create wireframes and prototypes for the Problem Library UI. Focus on user-friendly navigation and search functionality.
T1.notes: Ensure responsive design for different screen sizes.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle CRUD operations for problems. Implement authentication and authorization for secure access.
T2.notes: Ensure proper error handling and input validation.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational database schema to store problem details, tags, and metadata. Use an ORM for database interaction.
T3.notes: Optimize queries for faster search and retrieval.

T4.implementation_approach: Design a form-based UI for code submission with syntax highlighting and file upload support.
T4.notes: Include real-time validation for input fields.

T5.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to handle code submission, execution, and result retrieval. Use a sandbox environment for secure code execution.
T5.notes: Ensure security to prevent malicious code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a database schema to store code submissions, execution results, and timestamps.
T6.notes: Ensure data integrity and proper indexing for faster retrieval.

T7.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly profile page with sections for personal details, activity history, and achievements.
T7.notes: Focus on a clean and intuitive layout.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profiles, including CRUD operations and activity tracking.
T8.notes: Implement role-based access control for profile management.

T9.implementation_approach: Design a database schema to store user details, preferences, and activity logs.
T9.notes: Ensure scalability to handle a large number of users.

T10.implementation_approach: Design a leaderboard UI with sorting and filtering options. Include a search bar for user lookup.
T10.notes: Ensure real-time updates for leaderboard rankings.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data. Implement caching for faster response times.

T12.implementation_approach: Design a database schema to store leaderboard data, including user scores and rankings.
T12.notes: Use indexing to optimize sorting and filtering.

T13.implementation_approach: Design a UI for hints and tutorials with a categorized view and search functionality.
T13.notes: Ensure accessibility and readability of content.

T14.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and tutorials, including CRUD operations and search functionality.
T14.notes: Implement version control for tutorial updates.

T15.implementation_approach: Design a database schema to store hints, tutorials, and their metadata.
T15.notes: Ensure efficient storage and retrieval of large text data.

T16.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the Problem Library. Use mock data for testing.
T16.notes: Focus on edge cases and performance testing.

T17.implementation_approach: Test the code submission system for correctness, security, and performance. Use automated and manual testing.

T18.implementation_approach: Test the user profile functionality, including CRUD operations and activity tracking.

T19.implementation_approach: Test the leaderboard for real-time updates, sorting, and filtering. Use load testing tools to simulate high traffic.

T20.implementation_approach: Test the hints and tutorials functionality for content accuracy, search, and categorization.
T20.notes: Ensure content is displayed correctly across devices.

T21.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using a cloud service provider. Set up CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.
T21.notes: Ensure proper monitoring and logging for the deployed application.

files.content:
from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    tags = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=True)

    def __init__(self, title, description, difficulty, tags=None):
        self.title = title
        self.description = description
        self.difficulty = difficulty
        self.tags = tags

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Problem {self.title}>'

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_blueprints

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    # Application Configuration
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
    
    # Initialize Database
    db.init_app(app)
    
    # Register Blueprints
    register_blueprints(app)
    
    return app

code_repository.readme_content:
# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission System: A feature allowing users to submit code solutions and receive automated feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Profiles for users to track their progress, solved problems, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: A ranking system to display top users based on problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Tutorials: Guides and hints for solving problems to help users improve their skills.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
